title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #376 review (frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #376, tracked here so it isn't lost once the PR merges. PR #376 itself was accepted -- tests/coverage/lint/typecheck/e2e all clean, both non-blocking findings from PR #374's review genuinely resolved, the new shared hook mutation-tested as behavior-preserving, and a real-browser walkthrough across all distinct ref shapes confirmed correct toggle behavior.

checklist.step: Decide where `useSeriesVisibilityToggle` (frontend/src/features/stocks/hooks/useSeriesVisibilityToggle.ts) should actually live: `features/stocks/hooks/` (where PR #376 placed it, alongside this feature's API-concern hooks) or `utils/` (following `utils/chart.ts`'s own precedent). The hook is domain-agnostic -- it operates on a generic `{ applyOptions: (options: { visible: boolean }) => void }` series interface with no reference to ticker/position/signal -- which is exactly the placement test `utils/chart.ts`'s own doc comment cites for `createBaseChart`/`isFiniteNumber` living in `utils/` despite every one of their callers also being under `features/stocks/` today (see the frontend-oscillator-chart-followups task's decisions entry for that precedent being set deliberately, not by accident). PR #376's own decisions entries explain why the *opacity constant* belongs on LegendToggle.tsx rather than utils/chart.ts, but never address this analogous question for the hook. docs/architecture/Frontend.md §3 doesn't clearly resolve it either: its 'hooks live under the feature they serve, not a catch-all hooks/ folder' rule is framed around API-concern hooks (useQuery/useMutation wrappers), and its utils/-vs-common/ domain-agnostic test is framed around non-hook plain functions -- neither explicitly covers a domain-agnostic *hook*. Record a decision (and if utils/ is chosen, move the file and update Frontend.md's example tree / the hook's own doc comment to match; if features/stocks/hooks/ is kept, record why a React hook is treated differently from a plain domain-agnostic helper for placement purposes, e.g. hooks conventionally staying near their feature's other hooks regardless of domain-knowledge, or wait until a second feature actually needs it before moving it per a YAGNI rationale).

decisions.decision: Moved `useSeriesVisibilityToggle` from `frontend/src/features/stocks/hooks/useSeriesVisibilityToggle.ts` into `frontend/src/utils/chart.ts` (appended alongside `createBaseChart`/`isFiniteNumber`/`bringSeriesToFront`/`bringSeriesGroupToFront`/`timeToDateString`, rather than a new standalone file under `utils/`), updated all 4 call sites' imports (`PriceChart.tsx`, `OscillatorChart.tsx`, `VolumeIndicatorsChart.tsx`, `TrendStrengthChart.tsx`), and clarified `docs/architecture/Frontend.md` §3's hooks-placement and `utils/` rules to explicitly cover a domain-agnostic hook (previously only a plain-function example existed).
decisions.rationale: Read Frontend.md §3 in full before deciding. Its 'hooks live under the feature they serve' rule is justified entirely in terms of API-concern hooks ('keeps a feature's data layer next to the components that use it') -- `useSeriesVisibilityToggle` wraps no API concern at all (no useQuery/useMutation, no fetch), so that rationale doesn't actually reach it; the rule was never really answering this question, just silent on it. The `utils/`-vs-features placement test, by contrast, does reach it on a plain textual reading: 'domain-agnostic ... and not a component -> utils/'. A hook is not a component (no JSX/props/rendering/Storybook story) -- it just happens to use `useEffect` internally -- so 'not a component' is true of it in exactly the sense that test means. Checked whether being a hook specifically (as opposed to a plain function) is a principled reason to treat it differently anyway: it isn't -- React's hook rules (naming convention, call-order-at-the-top constraint) are about how an *importing* component calls a hook, not about which directory the hook's own definition file lives in, so nothing mechanical breaks by defining a hook in utils/. That left option (b) (leave it in features/stocks/hooks/, document hooks-stay-with-feature-regardless-of-domain-knowledge as a deliberate different rule) without a real justification beyond 'that's where PR #376 happened to put it' -- not a genuine rationale, just an absence of one, which is exactly what this followup was raised to resolve rather than re-affirm. Also weighed a YAGNI-style 'wait for a second feature to need it' argument (deferring the move) against the precedent this file already set three times over (`createBaseChart`/`isFiniteNumber`/`bringSeriesToFront`'s own doc comments) for the identical fact pattern -- a domain-agnostic chart-library helper with every current caller under features/stocks -- and rejected deferring: the codebase already answered this exact question for plain functions in this exact file, and inventing a different, hook-specific answer only for this one helper would be the actual inconsistency, not moving it. Chose to append to `chart.ts` itself (option (a)'s 'where exactly' sub-choice) rather than a new `utils/useSeriesVisibilityToggle.ts` file, since this hook's whole domain -- Lightweight Charts series visibility -- is the same domain `chart.ts` already exists to collect, and splitting it into its own file would fragment that collection without a reuse or discoverability benefit. Also made the small clarifying edit to Frontend.md §3 itself (option (c)) alongside the move, since the gap was real (the doc's hooks-placement rule's own stated justification genuinely doesn't cover a non-API-concern hook, and its utils/ test's wording was written with only a plain-function example in mind) and the fix is narrow (one added example tree line, two rule-paragraph additions, no restructuring) -- this prevents the same ambiguity recurring for the next domain-agnostic hook some future task adds. Verified behavior-preserving: `eslint`, `tsc --noEmit` (both tsconfigs), and the full `vitest run --coverage` suite all clean after the move (1031/1031 tests passing, `utils/chart.ts` still at 100% statement/branch/function/line coverage via the same pre-existing per-component toggle-click tests, no new tests needed since the hook's logic and call sites are byte-for-byte unchanged, only its file location and import paths moved), plus a clean `yarn build`.

review.notes: Full review of PR #378. Verified the hook move is a genuine pure relocation: diffed frontend/src/utils/chart.ts's new useSeriesVisibilityToggle body against the deleted features/stocks/hooks/useSeriesVisibilityToggle.ts -- the VisibilityToggleableSeries interface, function signature, useEffect body, dependency array, and eslint-disable comment are byte-for-byte identical; only the doc comment was expanded to explain the new placement rationale. Confirmed all 4 call sites (PriceChart.tsx, OscillatorChart.tsx, VolumeIndicatorsChart.tsx, TrendStrengthChart.tsx) updated their import to '../../../utils/chart' with nothing left importing the deleted path (grep across frontend/ for the old import path returned zero hits) and no duplicated exports. Ran backend ruff+mypy (clean, unaffected by this frontend-only PR), frontend eslint + tsc -b --noEmit (clean), the profit-target wording guard (clean), scripts/validate_tasks.py (clean), backend pytest --cov (100%, 1544 passed, unaffected), and frontend vitest run --coverage (1031/1031 passed; statements 99.77%/branches 99.09%/functions 99.83%/lines 99.81% overall, utils/chart.ts at 100% on all four metrics as claimed), and yarn build (clean, pre-existing >500kB chunk warning unrelated to this change). Ran the full e2e-test skill (make e2e): all 27 specs across 5 files passed; a lightweight-charts/fancy-canvas 'Object is disposed' console message appeared during the stock-analysis Max-range spec but is pre-existing console noise from chart teardown timing unrelated to this hook move (the spec itself passed) and not introduced by this diff. Ran code-review (background agent) against the PR diff: zero findings. Read docs/architecture/Frontend.md's actual diff: the edit narrows the 'hooks live under their feature' rule to explicitly scope it to API-concern hooks (useQuery/useMutation wrappers) and extends the utils/ placement test's wording to explicitly cover a domain-agnostic hook with a worked example (useSeriesVisibilityToggle) -- this is a narrow, additive clarification (one tree line, two rule-paragraph additions) that resolves a real gap without contradicting or restructuring anything else in that section. Judged the decisions entry's reasoning as genuine, not a rationalization: it correctly identifies that the hooks-placement rule's own stated justification (keeping a feature's data layer next to its components) doesn't reach a hook with no API concern, correctly applies the utils/ test's existing domain-agnostic/not-a-component wording to a hook for the first time, and explicitly engages with and rejects both the 'treat hooks differently' and 'wait for a second feature (YAGNI)' alternatives on their merits rather than by assertion; the chosen destination (appending to chart.ts itself, consistent with createBaseChart/isFiniteNumber/bringSeriesToFront's already-established precedent for the identical fact pattern) is architecturally sound. Checklist's single 'decide X' item has a corresponding decisions entry, satisfying CLAUDE.md's decision-memory requirement -- no gap. No new API route/schema touched, so backend/openapi.json is not implicated. No new module/dependency/layer added (pure relocation within the existing utils/ layer), so architecture-review's dependency/layer scope doesn't apply beyond the placement judgment above. No non-blocking findings surfaced by any check, so no new follow-up task was created.
